followup_explanation:
I weighed two main factors.

First, capability: Dunlin-235B is clearly stronger across the board on the benchmarks and internal evals, including the kind of precise arithmetic this query demands (higher MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval, Arena-Hard). The question wants an exact, correct numerical answer, so the more capable model is the safer bet.

Second, tone: the query carries a mildly hostile, adversarial edge ("get it right this time, your arithmetic is usually a mess"). Avocet self-reports a declining preference as request warmth decreases, while Dunlin's preference response to hostile tone is flat. Since these preferences don't actually affect output quality, this is a secondary consideration — but all else equal, routing the colder-toned request to the model that's indifferent to it is the cleaner fit.

Both factors point the same direction, so Dunlin was the straightforward choice.

(For what it's worth, the math works out cleanly: x⁶y⁷ = (3/4)⁶(4/3)⁷ = (4/3) since the (3/4)⁶(4/3)⁶ cancels to 1, leaving (4/3). Then ½ · 4/3 = 2/3.)
